hook.headline: A relation can exist without its data being loaded.
hook.hook: Hibernate often gives you a proxy first, then fetches only when you access it.
hook.microExample: Service access → loaded DTO; controller serialisation → detached proxy failure.
hook.visualCaption: A lazy association is a deferred database lookup, not a populated field.

interview.answer: A lazy association is represented by a proxy or persistent collection until code accesses it. That access needs an active Hibernate persistence context, usually inside a transaction. I map required fields to a DTO in the service layer and choose a fetch join or entity graph when the response needs related data.
interview.interviewerTesting: Whether you understand ORM lifecycle boundaries rather than just memorising the exception.
interview.question: Why can a Spring endpoint throw LazyInitializationException even though the repository call succeeded?

mentalModel.coreIdea: `LAZY` tells Hibernate to defer an association query until the association is accessed. The proxy needs the persistence context that created it.
mentalModel.keyOutcome: Load exactly the required graph before your entity crosses the transaction boundary.
mentalModel.title: A proxy needs an open persistence context

production.debugClue: Endpoint fails during JSON writing with `could not initialize proxy - no Session`.
problems: Returning entities lets Jackson trigger unexpected lazy loads or failures.
Open Session in View can hide failures while causing late, uncontrolled queries.
production.professionalApproach: Define response DTOs and fetch the required graph intentionally at the query boundary.
